synoptic.summary: The ridge over Utah flattens on Friday as a strong Pacific Northwest storm approaches, and the westerly flow aloft increases (23–25 kt from ~300° about 5,500 ft above the landings). Surface flow at the launches stays from 140°–150° all day Friday, and there is no afternoon switch to flow from 320°–360°. A weak trough crosses northern Utah Friday night into Saturday morning, mostly north of I-80, with light valley rain. Behind it, flow from 320°–340° runs 21–31 kt about 1,800 ft above the landings early Saturday and eases to ~10 kt by the afternoon. High pressure rebuilds Sunday with light flow from 130°–180° in the lowest levels. No thunderstorm risk in the period.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: This trough is eventually expected to cross northern Utah and southwest Wyoming Friday night into Saturday morning, bringing light valley rain/mountain snow to northern portions of the area, primarily north of I-80.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport (KSLC) sea-level pressure 1029.4 mb at 19:54 Thu, against 1028.1 mb 23 h earlier, so high pressure is holding for now. The forecast discussion expects the ridge to flatten Friday, then a brief trough passage Friday night and rising pressure behind it.

observations.summary: Thursday evening only (18:15–19:59 local), about 11 h before the first slot, so this says little about Friday morning. On the east side of Utah Valley, Spanish Fork and Alpine show flow from 006°–013° at 10–12 G12–14 kt. Lehi shows 128° at 6 G9 kt. Salt Lake airport is turning to 160° at 3 kt, as its airport forecast expects. Point of the Mountain and Draper returned no observations. South Valley Regional's newest report is 18:15 (2 h old).

Morning drainage is forecast, but from 150° instead of the usual 160°–200°.
